text.p: These are some of the leading stories in the official Vietnamese press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

-- The Vietnamese government has introduced new assessment procedures for overseas Vietnamese wanting to resettle in Vietnam. The procedures exclude "boatpeople" who have not been allowed to resettle in a third country or were expelled from the country of their last stay.

-- The National Drug Control and Prevention Committee says Vietnam has at least 180,000 drug addicts. Confirming that drug abuse has reached "alarming proportions", it said people under 30 accounted for 70 percent of those addicted.

-- The United Nations' World Food Programme amd the United Nations Development Programme will sign two projects worth $16.44 million with the Ministry of Agirculture and Rural Development on Tuesday to support small-holder forestry development in the five north-eastern provinces to reduce hunger and poverty.
-- Vietnam's government has issued a decision spelling out which individuals and organisations may use satellite dishes which can receive foreign television programmes.

-- Deputy Prime Minister Phan Van Khai told visiting governor of the Bank of France, Jean-Claude Trichet, that he hopes the bank will continue assisting Vietnam's banking system to develop and integrate in the world financial system.
-- Ho Chi Minh's Mausoleum will reopen from December 3, 1996 after a one-month routine closure for maintenance.
